_doc: The section cycle of the writing-workflow skill: w1 (proposal) -> r1 (mathematical review, fresh reader, prose
truth, and one owner review per principal statement, each a separate job) -> w2 (revision with a response
table) -> r2 (the same reviewers re-check against their own findings and the declined reasons) -> w3 (last
fixes) -> d (the driver recompiles the section, measures its pages and lists review coverage, then the delivery
review) -> verdict (STATUS = DELIVER or NOT YET). Units marked NOT YET go through rollout.fixup.example.json.
Every write stage compiles the section and measures that PDF, so a compile error or an overrun gets the writer's
one retry; every review stage first checks that the clause map has rows. Field table:
references/driver.md. Copy this file to <working repository>/rollout/ (init_campaign.py of lean-to-manuscript
does it), replace every SET-ME value, and run: rollout.py section-cycle.json --dry-run, then without --dry-run.
One config holds every unit of the manuscript; select with --only. First the opening part
(--only setting,principal), then the two pilots (--only F,C), then the other proof sections, and the
introduction last (--only intro), once the main theorems and principal statements have stopped moving.
Statements: the approved natural spine (spine) is the authority; the frozen contracts (contracts, clauses tagged
[clause:ID]) and the clause map are the record it must cover, read by owner and mathematical reviews.
The opening and introduction units are a generic split; F and C are the pilot sections of the Yang-Mills
campaign (2026). The labels (thm:A, thm:B, thm:RG, ...) are examples.
_protect_doc: Any change under a protected path fails the job and stops the run, whoever made it: with the manuscript protected, the editor integrates between runs, not during one. Build products do not count.

vars.manuscript: SET-ME: the canonical manuscript directory (main.tex, part1/, part2/, main.pdf)
vars.lean: SET-ME: the Lean source at the pinned commit
vars.graph_db: SET-ME: the dependency database built by lean-dependency-graph
vars.graph_hint: query the dependency database with sqlite3 -readonly {{graph_db}} (table nodes: name, kind, module, path, line, used); only rows with used = 1 count
vars.reader: an expert in the field who has read the opening part of the manuscript
vars.model_sections: the pilot sections the author approved
vars.disclosure: SET-ME: the disclosure wordings the author approved (honest-publication's assets/disclosure-wordings.md, filled in)
vars._vars_doc: w1_task, part_dir and unit_checks are overridden per unit: the opening part and the introduction have their own task and live in part1/; unit_checks are extra check commands for one unit's write stages. Every packet copies spine, contracts and clause_map, which must exist; clause_map names the file that holds the rows of the clause map: CLAUSE-MAP.tsv, or SPINE-NATURAL.md when the map is its section 6 (the build of every review stage fails on a map without a row). disclosure is read only by the introduction's task.

vars.contents: the conventions; the definitions needed to state the main theorems, in dependency order; the main theorems; remarks on what they do and do not claim and on the order in which the choices are made

principal.title: Principal statements and the proof of the main theorems

vars.contents: an overview of the architecture of the proof; the principal statements, each with the idea of its proof and a pointer to the section that proves it; the deduction of the main theorems from them; the table of constants and the order of their choice

vars.sources: the outline units of this section, their detailed notes, and the Lean they link

C._doc: Shown as a hard section whose page figure the author made a guide (L23): the allowance check only reports.
C.title: Path actions and the coupling reset

intro._doc: Written last. The owners of the main theorems check that the informal statements say what the formal ones say.
intro.title: Introduction

stages.name: w1
stages._check_doc: check_section.sh compiles the section with the manuscript's preamble and copies standalone.pdf and its log into the stage directory, replacing the writer's; check_allowance.py then measures that PDF. The same checks close w2, w3 and the fix-up's w4. Without latexmk, check_section.sh exits 3 (SKIPPED) and the stage fails: install TeX, or remove that command and accept that the pages measured are those of the writer's own PDF.

stages.name: d
stages._build_doc: Before freezing, the driver checks that the clause map has rows, recompiles standalone.pdf from the section file with the manuscript's preamble, measures the pages of that PDF against the allowance, and lists the statement labels that no earlier report names; the output is frozen as build.txt. A failing build stops the stage before any review. Without latexmk, check_section.sh exits 3 (SKIPPED), which stops it too: install TeX, or remove the compile command and accept that the PDF's provenance is not checked.
